rows.question: Within what period shall a Member State provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet - and on what does the start of that period depend?
rows.answer: 24 months after the entry into force of the implementing acts under Article 5a(23) AND Article 5c(6). The clock only starts running once BOTH acts are in force - not from the date of the Regulation. — Article 5a(1)

rows.question: Which paragraphs of Article 5a are the subject of the certification of the European Digital Identity Wallet under Article 5c?
rows.answer: Exactly four: paragraph 4 (user functions), paragraph 5 (technical requirements), paragraph 8 (validation mechanisms) and the logical separation under paragraph 14 - plus, where applicable, the standards under paragraph 24. — Article 5c(1)

rows.question: After how many months shall a suspended European Digital Identity Wallet be withdrawn if the security breach is not remedied?
rows.answer: After THREE months (Article 5e(2)). The same period applies under Article 10(3) to notified electronic identification schemes. — Article 5e(2)

rows.question: Which Articles do NOT apply to the European Digital Identity Wallet under Article 5a(22) - and which one applies by way of exception after all?
rows.answer: Articles 7, 9, 10, 12 and 12a do not apply. Article 11 (liability), however, applies mutatis mutandis via Article 5a(19). — Article 5a(19) and (22)

rows.question: May a relying party request more data than it indicated at registration?
rows.answer: No. Article 5b(3) expressly prohibits requesting data other than that indicated pursuant to paragraph 2, point (c). The registered scope is the maximum scope. — Article 5b(2)(c) and (3)

rows.question: From which assurance level onwards is recognition of a foreign electronic identification means mandatory?
rows.answer: From 'substantial'. At 'low', Article 6(2) provides only that recognition may take place. — Article 6(1)(b) and (2)

rows.question: What does Article 8(2) govern - obligations or definitions?
rows.answer: Definitions only. The three points (a) to (c) describe the scale low/substantial/high (decrease - decrease substantially - prevent). The actual obligation is in paragraph 3 and is addressed to the Commission. — Article 8(2) and (3)

rows.question: How long is a certification under Articles 5c, 12a and 30 valid - and subject to what condition?
rows.answer: Up to five years, provided that a vulnerability assessment is carried out every two years. Article 12a(3) additionally names a three-month period for remedying. — Article 5c(4), Article 12a(3), Article 30(3a)

rows.question: Who is liable for what under Article 11?
rows.answer: The notifying Member State for Article 7, points (d) and (f); the party issuing the electronic identification means for point (e); the party operating the authentication procedure for the incorrect operation under point (f) - in each case in cross-border transactions. — Article 11(1)-(3)

rows.question: How does the burden of proof differ between qualified and non-qualified trust service providers?
rows.answer: With non-qualified TSPs the person who suffered the damage shall prove intention or negligence. With a QTSP both are presumed - it has to exonerate itself. — Article 13(1), second and third subparagraphs

rows.question: What is the maximum level of administrative fines under Article 16?
rows.answer: At least EUR 5 000 000 for natural persons, or for legal persons EUR 5 000 000 or 1 % of the total worldwide turnover of the preceding year - whichever is higher. A separate framework for European Digital Identity Wallet providers does NOT exist in eIDAS. — Article 16(2)

rows.question: When does the 24-hour notification deadline start running for a TSP and when for a QTSP?
rows.answer: For the non-qualified TSP from BECOMING AWARE (Article 19a(1)(b)), for the QTSP from THE INCIDENT (Article 24(2)(fb)). The QTSP is thus held to the stricter standard. — Article 19a(1)(b) and Article 24(2)(fb)

rows.question: At what intervals is a QTSP audited and how quickly shall the report be available?
rows.answer: At least every 24 months, at its own expense. The conformity assessment report shall be submitted to the supervisory body within THREE WORKING DAYS of its receipt. — Article 20(1)

rows.question: What obligation does a QTSP have before a planned audit - new since eIDAS 2.0?
rows.answer: It shall inform the supervisory body at least one month in advance and shall allow it to participate as an observer upon request. — Article 20(1a)

rows.question: May a GDPR infringement cost a provider its eIDAS qualified status?
rows.answer: Yes. Under Article 20(3b) the supervisory body shall withdraw the status where the data protection supervisory authorities report an infringement and this is justified by the extent, duration and consequences. The same applies under paragraph 3a to NIS2 infringements. — Article 20(3a) and (3b)

rows.question: From what point in time may a service be provided as 'qualified'?
rows.answer: Only after the qualified status has been indicated in the trusted list under Article 22(1) - not already upon the supervisory body's decision. — Article 21(3)

rows.question: Which four methods of identity verification does Article 24(1a) permit?
rows.answer: (a) European Digital Identity Wallet or notified electronic identification means with assurance level high, (b) certificate of a qualified electronic signature or of a qualified electronic seal issued in compliance with (a), (c) or (d), (c) other methods ensuring a high level of confidence and confirmed by a conformity assessment body, (d) physical presence. — Article 24(1a)

rows.question: How does Article 24(1b) differ from paragraph (1a)?
rows.answer: Paragraph 1b concerns the verification of ATTRIBUTES and provides five methods instead of four - additionally permitted is the qualified electronic attestation of attributes (point (c)). — Article 24(1a) and (1b)

rows.question: Why is point (i) in Article 24(2) followed directly by point (k)?
rows.answer: Point (j) was deleted by eIDAS 2.0. The gap in the lettering is intentional. — Article 24(2)

rows.question: Within what period shall a revocation of a certificate be published, and from when does it take effect?
rows.answer: Within 24 hours of receipt of the request. The revocation becomes effective immediately upon its publication. — Article 24(3)

rows.question: How many types of qualified services does Article 24a list?
rows.answer: Eleven - from qualified electronic signatures and qualified electronic seals (paragraph 1) through to qualified electronic ledgers (paragraph 11). — Article 24a(1)-(11)

rows.question: What legal effect does a QES have, and what legal effect a qualified electronic seal?
rows.answer: The QES has the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten signature (Article 25(2)). The qualified electronic seal enjoys the presumption of integrity of the data and of correctness of the origin of that data (Article 35(2)) - it does not replace a signature. — Article 25(2) and Article 35(2)

rows.question: What is the difference between Article 26, point (c), and Article 36, point (c)?
rows.answer: Article 26(c) requires the SOLE control of the signatory over the electronic signature creation data; Article 36(c) requires of the creator of a seal only 'its control'. — Article 26(1)(c) and Article 36(1)(c)

rows.question: What changes for remote signing under eIDAS 2.0 - and by when?
rows.answer: The management of remote qualified electronic signature and seal creation devices becomes a qualified trust service in its own right under Article 29a and Article 39a respectively. The grandfathering under Article 51(3) ends on 21 May 2026. — Article 29(1a), Article 29a, Article 39a, Article 51(3)

rows.question: How many copies of the electronic signature creation data may a remote signature service keep?
rows.answer: Only as many as are STRICTLY NECESSARY to ensure continuity of the service - and they shall be at the same security level as the originals. — Article 29a(1)(b)(i) and (ii)

rows.question: How many points does validation check under Article 32, and how many under Article 32a?
rows.answer: Article 32 checks eight points ((a) to (h)), Article 32a only seven ((a) to (g)). Precisely the QSCD condition in Article 32(1), point (f), is missing. — Article 32(1) and Article 32a(1)

rows.question: Shall a qualified electronic time stamp bear a qualified signature?
rows.answer: No. Article 42(1), point (c), requires an ADVANCED electronic signature or an advanced electronic seal of the QTSP - or some equivalent method. — Article 42(1)(c)

rows.question: Which four presumptions does a qualified electronic registered delivery service (ERDS) trigger?
rows.answer: Integrity of the data, the sending of that data by the identified sender, its receipt by the identified addressee, and the accuracy of the date and time of sending and receipt. — Article 43(2)

rows.question: Which signature level does Article 44 require for securing the sending/receiving process, and which for the point in time?
rows.answer: Point (d) requires an advanced electronic signature or an advanced electronic seal; point (f), by contrast, requires a QUALIFIED electronic time stamp. — Article 44(1)(d) and (f)

rows.question: Which two obligations does Article 45(1a) impose on providers of web-browsers?
rows.answer: They shall recognise QWACs AND display the attested identity data in a user-friendly manner. Microenterprises and small enterprises during their first five years of operation are exempt. — Article 45(1a)

rows.question: Under what conditions may a provider of a web-browser take precautionary measures against a QWAC?
rows.answer: Only in the event of substantiated concerns related to a security breach or a loss of integrity - and it shall notify this in writing without undue delay to the Commission, the supervisory body, the certificate holder and the issuing QTSP. — Article 45a(2) and (3)

rows.question: Does an electronic attestation of attributes replace electronic identification?
rows.answer: In principle, no. Article 45c expressly prohibits this unless the Member State has specifically allowed it - in which case qualified EAAs from other Member States are also accepted. — Article 45c

rows.question: Which signature level does Annex V require for the QEAA - and what does Annex I require at the same point?
rows.answer: Annex V, point (g), requires a QUALIFIED electronic signature or a qualified electronic seal of the QTSP. Annex I, point (g), requires at the same point only an advanced electronic signature. — Annex I(g) and Annex V(g)

rows.question: How many attributes does the minimum list in Annex VI comprise?
rows.answer: Eleven: address, age, gender, civil status, family composition, nationality, educational qualifications, professional qualifications, powers and mandates, public permits and licences, and - for legal persons only - financial and company data. — Annex VI

rows.question: What distinguishes a PuB-EAA from a QEAA?
rows.answer: The PuB-EAA is issued by a public sector body responsible for an authentic source within the meaning of Article 3(46) and meets Annex VII. That body needs no QTSP status, but shall demonstrate a level of reliability and trustworthiness in accordance with Article 24 and is notified together with a conformity assessment report. — Article 45f(1)-(3), Annex VII

rows.question: Which providers of electronic attestations of attributes shall provide an interface with the European Digital Identity Wallet?
rows.answer: Only providers of QUALIFIED electronic attestations of attributes (Article 45g(2)) and public sector bodies within the meaning of Article 3(46) (Article 45f(8)). The obligation under Article 45g(1) (request, obtain, store, manage), by contrast, applies to all providers of electronic attestations of attributes. — Article 45f(8), Article 45g(1) and (2)

rows.question: Whose data shall a provider of electronic attestations of attributes not combine with EAA data under Article 45h?
rows.answer: Data from other services offered by it ITSELF OR BY ITS COMMERCIAL PARTNERS. The provision thus reaches beyond the provider's own group. — Article 45h(1)

rows.question: How do the preservation service (Article 34) and the archiving service (Article 45j) differ?
rows.answer: Article 34 extends the trustworthiness of a qualified SIGNATURE beyond its technological validity period. Article 45j ensures the durability, legibility and integrity of the DOCUMENTS throughout the legal or contractual preservation period. — Articles 34 and 45j

rows.question: Which signature level does the integrity report of a qualified electronic archiving service require?
rows.answer: A QUALIFIED electronic signature or a qualified electronic seal (Article 45j(1), point (d)) - unlike the validation service under Article 33(1), point (b), where an advanced one suffices. — Article 45j(1)(d)

rows.question: What does Article 45k(2) presume for qualified electronic ledgers?
rows.answer: The unique and accurate sequential chronological ordering and the integrity of the data records - not their substantive correctness. — Article 45k(2)

rows.question: Which Articles were deleted by eIDAS 2.0 and where is their content found today?
rows.answer: Article 17 (supervisory body), Article 18 (mutual assistance) and Article 19 (security requirements). Their successors are Article 46b, Article 46d and Article 19a in conjunction with Article 24(2), points (fa) and (fb). — Articles 17-19 (repealed)

rows.question: Which three deadlines does Article 51 name for 21 May 2026?
rows.answer: Paragraph 2: end of the continued validity of old qualified certificates. Paragraph 3: end of the grandfathering for the management of remote signature/seal creation devices without qualified status. Paragraph 4: submission of a CAR on compliance with Article 24(1), (1a) and (1b). 21 May 2027 applies only to old SSCDs under paragraph 1. — Article 51(1)-(4)

rows.question: What intensity of supervision applies to QTSPs and what to non-qualified TSPs?
rows.answer: QTSPs are supervised both ex ante AND ex post. Non-qualified TSPs only ex post - and then only where the supervisory body is informed of an alleged failure to comply. — Article 46b(3)(a) and (b)
